Rashi on Chullin 2b:1:1.hebrew: אבל אמר הרי עלי לא - דלמא פשע ולא מקיים, והכי מוקמינן לה בנדרים בפ"ק (דף י.), לר' יהודה תני נודב ומשלם. אלמא מעריכין ונודרין לכתחלה לא, דהרי עלי הוא דליכא למימר בהו הרי זו, עד דאמר ברישא ערכי עלי והדר יהיב כפי הקצוב בפרשה, ודמי עלי נמי דבעי למשיימיה כעבדא, דהיכי מצי למימר הרי אלו לערכים אם לא נדר תחלה בערך:
Rashi on Chullin 2b:1:1.english: But if he said, "It is incumbent upon me" - no - [This is] lest he be negligent and not fulfill it. And thus we establish it in [tractate] Nedarim, in the first chapter (10a): according to Rabbi Yehuda, [the mishna] is taught [with the emended wording], "one who donates [a specific item] and pays." This shows that [the mishna's rulings that] 'they value' and 'they vow' do not [indicate that this is permitted] ab initio, for it is [only when he says] 'it is incumbent upon me' [that this applies] - since one cannot say about these [valuation-vows], 'this is hereby,' unless he first says, 'my valuation is incumbent upon me,' and only afterward gives according to the amount fixed in the [Torah] portion. And likewise [with] 'the value [of a person] is incumbent upon me' - since it needs to be appraised like [that of] a slave, for how could he say, 'these are hereby for valuation,' if he did not first vow using the term 'valuation'?

Rashi on Chullin 2b:2:1.english: But is [the word] 'all' not [used only] for something done ab initio - That is, is there no [usage of] 'all' that refers to something [permitted] ab initio (lechatchila)?

Rashi on Chullin 2b:2:2.hebrew: הכל חייבים בסוכה - לאתויי קטן שאינו צריך לאמו:
Rashi on Chullin 2b:2:2.english: All are obligated in [the mitzvah of] sukkah - This comes to include a minor who does not need his mother [i.e., who is old enough to be looked after by others].

Rashi on Chullin 2b:2:3.hebrew: הכל חייבים בציצית - לאתויי קטן היודע להתעטף:
Rashi on Chullin 2b:2:3.english: All are obligated in tzitzit - This comes to include a minor who knows how to wrap himself [in a garment].

Rashi on Chullin 2b:3:1.hebrew: חייבין לא קאמינא - היכא דתני חייבין, מוכח ודאי דלכתחלה קאמר:
Rashi on Chullin 2b:3:1.english: I did not say 'obligated' - Wherever [the Mishnah] teaches 'obligated,' it certainly proves that it is speaking of [what is permitted] ab initio.

Rashi on Chullin 2b:3:2.hebrew: לאתויי יורש. והא ודאי לכתחלה קאמר, דמצוה רמיא עליה על כרחיה:
Rashi on Chullin 2b:3:2.english: All lay hands - This comes to include an heir [who inherits an animal designated for sacrifice]. And this is certainly stated as a lechatchila (optimal) requirement, for the mitzvah is incumbent upon him whether he wants it or not.

Rashi on Chullin 2b:5:1.hebrew: תרתי דיעבד למה לי - הכי איבעי ליה למיתני: שחיטת הכל כשרה, חוץ מחש"ו, דמשמע שפיר דהנך דמרבינן מהכל דיעבד קמרבינן, אבל לא לכתחלה. א"נ, ניתני הכל שוחטין לחודיה, כדתנן גבי מעריכין ונודרין, ולא מפרש, למה לי למיתני הכל שוחטין ואצטריך לפרושי ושחיטתן כשרה למימר דשוחטין דרישא דיעבד הוא. ואי קשיא: בתמורה נמי הא תני והדר מפרש - התם לא קתני כה"ג הכל ממירין ותמורתן תמורה בהדי הדדי. ואי משום לא שאדם רשאי, משום דבעי לאסוקי וסופג את הארבעים, לאשמועינן דלוקין על לאו שאין בו מעשה:
Rashi on Chullin 2b:5:1.english: Why do I need two [expressions of] after the fact - This is how it should rather have taught: 'The slaughter of all is valid, except for a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor,' which would imply well that those [disqualified people] whom we include from [the word] 'all' we include [only] after the fact, but not ab initio. Alternatively, let it teach 'All may slaughter' by itself, as we learned regarding those who valuate and those who vow, without explaining [further] - [then there would be no difficulty, since one could ask] why it needed to teach 'All may slaughter' [without elaborating, as elsewhere] - and [instead] it needed to explain 'and their slaughter is valid,' in order to say that the 'may slaughter' of the first clause means after the fact. [That is the two expressions of 'after the fact.'] And if you should ask: but in [tractate] Temurah too, it teaches [a phrase] and afterward explains it - there, it does not teach in this manner, [namely] 'All may effect a substitution' and 'their substitution is a valid substitution,' as two parallel statements. And if [you would say this is] because of '[though] a person is not permitted [to do so],' [that phrase appears there] because it wants to arrive at '[and] he receives forty lashes,' to teach us that one is lashed for a prohibition that involves no action.

Tosafot on Chullin 2b:1:1.hebrew: אבל אמר הרי עלי לא - הך סוגיא כלישנא בתרא דפ"ק דנדרים (דף י.) דקאמר דפליגי בנודב, אבל ללישנא קמא דקאמר דפליגי בנודר, אבל בנודב מודה רבי מאיר. וא"ת: כיון דקרא בנדר כתיב, מנא ליה לרבי מאיר דאין נודב טוב מנודר ומשלם? ולרבי יהודה נמי אמאי, אם אמר הרי עלי לא? הא כל היכא דכתיב נדר הוי נדר דוקא, ונדבה הוי נדבה דוקא, כדמוכח בריש מנחות (דף ב.) וזבחים (דף ב.) גבי "כאשר נדרת לה' אלהיך נדבה", דפריך: האי נדבה? נדר הוא! וי"מ דהתם פריך משום דשני קרא בדבוריה, וי"ל דקסבר כיון דחייש קרא לתקלה בנדר, ה"ה בנדבה, דהא איכא למיחש לתקלה, דאפי' מביאה לעזרה ומקדישה, יכול להנות ולמעול בה ולבא לידי תקלה בכמה עניינים, דכ"ע לא בקיאי כהלל, דמעולם לא מעל אדם בעולתו (פסחים דף סו:). ולרבי יהודה נמי משמע ליה קרא דוקא בנדבה, אע"ג דבנדר כתיב, דהא בנדר לא מצי למימר דנודר ומשלם טוב, שהרי כתיב "וכי תחדל לנדור לא יהיה בך חטא", הא אם תדור יהיה בך חטא. וללישנא קמא דנדרים מפרשינן לקרא: הא אם תדור אפשר שיהיה בך חטא אם לא תשלם. וא"ת: לרבי מאיר, דאין טוב שיהא נודב ומשלם כל עיקר, אפילו מביא כבשתו לעזרה, להאי לישנא בתרא דנדרים, היאך אכלו ישראל שלמים במדבר? וי"ל, כיון שנאסרו בענין אחר בבשר, הוו כאילו צוה להם המקום לאכול על ידי שלמים. וא"ת: והא כתיב (בראשית כ״ח:כ׳) "וידר יעקב נדר", וכתיב (יונה ב׳:י׳) "את אשר נדרתי אשלמה"? וי"ל, דבשעת צרה שרי, כדאמרינן בבראשית רבה: "וידר יעקב נדר" - "לאמר לאמר" - לדורות, שיהיו נודרים בעת צרה:
Tosafot on Chullin 2b:1:1.english: But if he said, "It is incumbent upon me," it is not [valid to substitute] - This sugya follows the latter version (lishna basra) [of the dispute] in the first chapter of Nedarim (10a), which states that they disagree in the case of one who makes a donation (nodev). But according to the first version (lishna kama), which states that they disagree in the case of one who takes a vow (noder), in the case of a donor Rabbi Meir concedes [that he need not bring a replacement if it is lost]. And if you should ask: since the verse is written regarding a vow (neder), how does Rabbi Meir know that a donor is not [treated as] better than one who vows and [must therefore] pay [a replacement]? And according to Rabbi Yehuda too, why is it that if one says "It is incumbent upon me," it is not [valid to substitute]? For wherever "neder" is written it means specifically a neder, and "nedavah" means specifically a nedavah, as is proven at the beginning of Menachot (2a) and Zevachim (2a), regarding [the phrase] "as you vowed to the Lord your God, a donation (nedavah)" - for it asks there: is this a nedavah? It is a neder! And some explain that the question is asked there because the verse switches its own wording [inconsistently]. But [Tosafot] answer that [Rabbi Meir] holds that since the verse is concerned about mishap in the case of a neder, the same applies to a nedavah - for there, too, there is cause for concern about mishap: even if one brings [the animal] to the Temple courtyard and consecrates it, he can [still] derive benefit from it and commit trespass (me'ilah) with it, and come to mishap in many ways, since not everyone is as expert as Hillel, who never trespassed with his own burnt-offering (Pesachim 66b). And for Rabbi Yehuda too, the verse implies to him [that it refers] specifically to a nedavah, even though it is written regarding a neder - for in the case of a neder he cannot say that one who vows and [then] pays [a replacement] is "good," since it is written, "but if you refrain from vowing, there will be no sin in you" - implying that if you do vow, there will be sin in you. And according to the first version (lishna kama) of Nedarim, we interpret the verse [differently]: that if you vow, it is possible that there will be sin in you, if you do not pay [what you vowed]. And if you should ask: according to Rabbi Meir, that there is no "good" whatsoever in one who donates and [then must] pay [a replacement if it is lost] - even where he had [already] brought his lamb to the [Temple] courtyard - then according to this latter version of Nedarim, how did the Israelites eat peace-offerings (shelamim) in the wilderness? And [Tosafot] answer: since they were forbidden [to eat] meat in any other way, it was as though the Omnipresent had commanded them to eat by means of peace-offerings [so that it was not treated as an ordinary, avoidable donation]. And if you should ask: but is it not written (Genesis 28:20), "And Jacob vowed a vow," and is it not written (Jonah 2:10), "That which I vowed I will pay"? And [Tosafot] answer: that in a time of distress it is permitted [to vow], as we say in Bereishit Rabbah: "'And Jacob vowed a vow, saying (leimor)'" - [the doubled expression] "leimor, leimor" [comes] to [teach] for [future] generations, that they should make vows in a time of distress.

Rashi on Chullin 2b:6:1.hebrew: הכי קתני - לכתחלה ודיעבד דמתניתין, הכל שוחטין לכתחלה, לאתויי טמא בחולין:
Rashi on Chullin 2b:6:1.english: This is what it teaches - [Regarding] the ab initio and after the fact [distinction] of our Mishnah: "All may slaughter" [is stated] ab initio, to include a tamei person [slaughtering] non-sacred food.

Rashi on Chullin 2b:6:2.english: It is obvious - For Israel was not commanded regarding the purity of their non-sacred food (chulin).

Rashi on Chullin 2b:6:3.hebrew: שנעשו על טהרת קדש - דקבל עליה לאכול בטהרת קדש, שרוצה להרגיל עצמו בטהרת קדשים, שאם יאכל שלמים או תודה יהא בקי בשמירתן:
Rashi on Chullin 2b:6:3.english: That were made in the purity of sacred [food] - [Meaning] that he accepted upon himself to eat [non-sacred food] in the purity required for sacred [food], because he wants to accustom himself to the purity [required] for sacred items, so that if he [later] eats peace-offerings or a thanksgiving-offering, he will be expert in observing their [purity laws].

Rashi on Chullin 2b:6:4.hebrew: כקדש דמו - וחייב להבדל מדרבנן מכל טומאות הפוסלות בהן, ואפילו הכי (שחיט טמא) לכתחלה ובסכין ארוכה, כדמפרש:
Rashi on Chullin 2b:6:4.english: Its blood is like that of a consecrated animal - and one is obligated by rabbinic law to keep away, with respect to it, from all the impurities that disqualify [offerings]. Even so, (a tamei person may slaughter it) ab initio, and with a long knife, as [the Gemara] will explain.

Rashi on Chullin 2b:8:1.hebrew: ובמוקדשין - לכתחלה לא ישחוט, ואפילו בסכין ארוכה, כיון דמוזהר מן התורה שלא יטמא, כדכתיב (במדבר יח) "ואני הנה נתתי לך את משמרת תרומותי", אלמא בעינן שמירה, גזור בהו רבנן לכתחלה, משום "לך לך" אמרינן נזירא: "סחור סחור, לכרמא לא תקרב":
Rashi on Chullin 2b:8:1.english: And with consecrated animals - Ab initio he should not slaughter, even with a long knife, since he is enjoined by the Torah not to become impure, as it is written (Numbers 18): "And I, behold, I have given you charge of My terumot" — implying that guarding [against impurity] is required. The Sages decreed against it ab initio, because of [the principle]: "Go away, go away," we say to the nazirite, "go around, go around, do not approach the vineyard."

Tosafot on Chullin 2b:5:1.hebrew: אנא שחיטתן כשרה קא קשיא לי - משמע שרב אשי הקשה אותה קושיא, ואע"פ שהיא סוגיית הגמרא, ומכאן ראיה שרב אשי סידר הגמרא. אע"ג דאביי ורבא נמי אתו לשנויי הך קושיא, והם קדמו הרבה לרב אשי, שמא גם בימיהם הקשוה כבר:
Tosafot on Chullin 2b:5:1.english: I am troubled by [the phrase] "their slaughter is valid" - This implies that it was Rav Ashi himself who raised this difficulty, even though it is [already part of] the Gemara's own discussion; and from here there is proof that Rav Ashi redacted the Gemara. Even though Abaye and Rava also came to resolve this very difficulty, and they preceded Rav Ashi by a great deal - perhaps even in their days this difficulty had already been raised.

Tosafot on Chullin 2b:6:1.hebrew: טמא בחולין מאי למימרא - ואע"ג דאסור לגרום טומאה לחולין שבא"י, היינו דוקא בפירות דשייכא בהו תרומה, אבל בשר לא. ואפילו יהא אסור לטמאות גופו באוכלין טמאין, כדדרשינן: "והתקדשתם והייתם קדושים" - אזהרה לבני ישראל שיאכלו חוליהן בטהרה, מכל מקום יכול לטמאותן ולאוכלן בימי טומאתו:
Tosafot on Chullin 2b:6:1.english: A tamei person [and] non-sacred food, what does this come to teach? - Even though it is forbidden to cause impurity to non-sacred produce in the Land of Israel, that is specifically with regard to produce, since teruma applies to it, but not to meat. And even if it should be forbidden for a person to render his own body impure by eating impure foods - as we derive from "You shall sanctify yourselves and be holy," a warning to the Children of Israel that they should eat their non-sacred food in purity - nevertheless, he may render it impure and eat it during the days of his impurity.
